rv.q: This 'Menagerie' promises to be the most revealing revival of a cornerstone classic for many a year to come.
In whisks Cherry Jones’s Amanda, and the spell is cast.
Tennessee Williams' world of poetry and prose is presented gracefully, even wondrously, in this distinctive production.
This is a fine evening at the theater, not a divine revelation.
It is, like the work itself, unforgettable.
No matter how archetypal these characters and familiar their experiences, when played with such subtlety and emotional veracity, they yield lingering rewards in the sad music of memory.
This radiant Menagerie will also leave a glow in your heart.
Get to this brilliant, brilliant production.
It’s a remarkably satisfying trip to a disturbing destination.
It seems fitting that this performance, and this production, will really exist only in memory – but there it will lodge.
Warm and touchingly humane, she anchors the near perfect quartet
Tiffany has stripped Tennessee Williams's 1944 career-maker of any extraneous elements and delivered it to us, fresh, alive, and powerful.

cn.t: John Tiffany's stunning revival breathes fresh life into Williams' classic, anchored by Cherry Jones's remarkable performance as Amanda and a uniformly excellent cast that delivers the play's poetry and emotional truth with delicate strength.

sg.ra: The Booth is one of Broadway's smallest houses at 766 seats, so center orchestra rows C-H give close-up detail of plays and intimate dramas without paying the very-front premium. Row AA front offers max legroom (Headout) but stage is high; step back a few rows for better sightline onto the stage floor.

sg.vl: Workable angle, not the sweet spot
sg.ra: Booth is narrow so side orchestra remains viable, but a 2018 BWW forum post specifically flagged 'angle from the front side seats' as a concern. Closer rows (BB, A) on the side get awkward angles onto the high stage. Mid-house aisle seats recover the view while adding legroom.
sg.rr: A-P (17 rows, odd 1-15 left, even 2-16 right)

sg.ra: In a 252-seat mezzanine with only 8 rows, even the back row is close. SeatPlan and Headout both call Center Mezz A-B some of the best seats in the house, and G-H are cited as strong value. With the Booth's intimate scale, the mezzanine never feels distant — this is the value pick.

sg.vl: Small house saves the side angle
sg.ra: SeatPlan explicitly notes side-mezz views are 'slightly more angled but still viable' because the Booth is narrow. Decent budget alternative, but the center mezz is a better value at similar price tier so this is solid-not-sweet.
